newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: S&P considers change in Argentine sovereign rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P considers change in Argentine sovereign rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's, the world's largest credit rating agency, said Wednesday it is considering a change in Argentina's sovereign debt rating within two to three weeks.

Leo O'Neill, president and chief ratings officer of S&P told journalists the agency has three options -- It can upgrade the outlook on Argentina's BB- rating, upgrade the debt or maintain the current rating.
S&P's outlook on Argentine debt is currently 'stable.'
"There are three potential outcomes (of the review). Two of them are favorable, one of them is neutral. I don't want to create an environment where everybody is expecting an upgrade," O'Neill said.

However, asked about the review he said: "Well, clearly the reason why we are here today speaks for itself - we have confidence in Argentina - the Convertibility survived the test of the Tequila effect, the economy has recovered very sharply since then."
The president was in Buenos Aires to announce the acquisition by S&P of the local rating agency Risk Annalysis.
He said S&P was currently meeting with government officials to discuss the review.

O'Neill added that in its consideration of a change in the sovereign rating, "we are coming to grips with the steadiness" of Argentine economic policy now, in comparison with the economic history of the country. "Its history is not the future," he said.
Argentina suffered from hyperinflation at the end of the 1980s with annual consumer prices rising to nearly 5,000 percent in 1989 but now virtually has no inflation.
